Implementation Plan

Plan for the security finding: a fork PR named `ai/issue-*` can hold up the merge train

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `cef983cf9024c5bb6350d9fe46e529187c749493`, branch `ai/issue-4701`, which matches the integration branch metadata (no mismatch).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends _mt_blockers_for_into
Scope-mode justification: The finding names one defect: `_mt_blockers_for_into` (`scripts/review_merge_train.sh:212-244`) treats any older open PR whose head ref starts with `ai/issue-` as a blocker. It never checks which repository the head lives in. Any GitHub user can open a fork PR with a head branch called `ai/issue-<n>`, edit a popular file, and hold a later same-repository `ai/issue-*` PR in `ai:merge-queued` for as long as the fork PR stays open. The fix extends two existing pieces: the open-PR listing (`_mt_list_open_prs`, lines 194-204) and the blocker filter. Both `gate` (line 340) and `release` (line 681) already use that filter, so both are fixed together. The fix adds no API call, because `head.repo.full_name` is already in the `pulls?state=open` response the script fetches. By the Boil the Lake rule, the complete version costs only a few lines more than the shortcut. It also stops fork PRs from using up the `MERGE_TRAIN_MAX_OLDER_PRS` examination cap, which is the same defect class (§6: correctness and safety over speed). I am not adding new release-side dispatch filtering. A fork PR cannot normally be queued, and `review_autofix.yml` already skips fork PRs before review (agents.md, "Fork, missing-repo and invalid-head PRs skip both review…").

1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/review_merge_train.sh`
  - `_mt_list_open_prs`: add `head_repo: (.head.repo.full_name // "")` to the per-PR compact JSON object in the `--jq` projection. A deleted fork reports `head.repo` as null, so it becomes `""`. Update the comment above it, which lists the fields `{number, head, base, draft, labels[]}`, to include `head_repo`.
  - `_mt_blockers_for_into`:
    - Read `head_repo` from each line, next to the existing `jq -r` reads.
    - After the `${MT_PREFIX}` check and before the draft and label checks, compare it to `MT_REPO`. Lowercase both sides with bash `${var,,}` because GitHub owner and repo names are case-insensitive.
    - On a mismatch or an empty value, log `MERGE_TRAIN_FOREIGN_HEAD_SKIPPED pr=<pr> older=<num>` and `continue`. Leave the attacker-controlled repo name out of the log.
    - This check must come before `examined=$((examined + 1))`. Otherwise fork PRs could use up `MT_MAX_OLDER` and push real same-repository blockers out of the examined window.
    - Update the function's header comment to "Older open same-repository ai/issue-* PRs …".
  - Script header policy comment (lines 13-18): say that blockers must be same-repository heads, and that fork heads are never blockers.
- `tests/test_review_merge_train.py`
  - Change the `_pr(...)` helper to add `"repo": {"full_name": head_repo}` under `"head"`, using a new keyword parameter `head_repo: str | None = "acme/consumer"`. The default matches the `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` the tests set, so every existing test keeps its current meaning. Passing `None` gives `"repo": None`, which models a deleted fork.
  - Add these tests:
    - (a) `test_gate_ignores_older_fork_pr_with_ai_issue_head`: an older fork PR `_pr(4075, "ai/issue-4063", head_repo="evil/consumer")` overlaps the current PR's files. Expect `result=unblocked`, no `AUTOFIX_MERGE_QUEUED`, no `pulls/4075/files` call in the log, and `MERGE_TRAIN_FOREIGN_HEAD_SKIPPED pr=4077 older=4075` in stdout.
    - (b) Deleted-fork case (`head_repo=None`): also not a blocker.
    - (c) Case-insensitive match: `head_repo="Acme/Consumer"` is still a blocker, so the PR is queued.
    - (d) Fork PRs don't use up the cap: `MERGE_TRAIN_MAX_OLDER_PRS=1`, an older fork PR plus an older overlapping same-repository PR. Expect the PR to be queued with `blockers=#<same-repo>`.
    - (e) Release: a queued same-repository PR whose only overlapping older PR is a fork. Expect `MERGE_TRAIN_RELEASED` and a dispatch.
- `README.md`: in the `MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED` row (line 119) and the merge-train `gate` table row (around line 2290), change "older open `ai/issue-*` PR" to "older open same-repository `ai/issue-*` PR (fork heads are never blockers)".
- `agents.md`: in workflow-architecture item 7, change "older open `ai/issue-*` PRs on the same base" to "older open same-repository `ai/issue-*` PRs on the same base".
- `docs/INVENTORY.md` line 230: make the same wording change.
- New changelog fragment `changelog.d/6500-merge-train-fork-blockers.md`, under `<!-- changelog: security -->`, in the format of `changelog.d/4618-sweep-dispatch-default-branch.md`. It closes security finding `fork-pr-blocks-merge-train` (high, STRIDE DoS) and should include a "The numbers that matter" table with 0 new API calls. The finding body (`Refs #3576`) gives no issue number, so 6500 is an assumption taken from the AI-memory record "Issue #6500 is clear". The implementer should use the real issue number if it is known at implement time.

2. Functions or modules to implement
- No new functions. Only `_mt_list_open_prs` and `_mt_blockers_for_into` change. The `_mt_blockers_for` printing wrapper and the `_mt_gate` / `_mt_release` callers stay unchanged; they get the fix through the shared helper.

3. Data structures affected
- The per-PR JSON line from `_mt_list_open_prs` gains one additive field, `head_repo` (string, possibly empty). Other consumers read fields by name with `jq -r '.number'` and similar, so an extra key is harmless.
- The release loop also reads `prs_json`. It does not use `head_repo`; behaviour there is unchanged apart from the shared blocker filter.

4. API or interface changes
- No CLI, environment-variable, or label changes, and no new GitHub API calls: `head.repo.full_name` comes from the existing paginated `GET repos/{repo}/pulls?state=open…`.
- New stable log line: `MERGE_TRAIN_FOREIGN_HEAD_SKIPPED pr=<n> older=<m>`. It is additive; existing log keys are not renamed.

## Decisions
### D1 — Same-repository check as the authorization criterion
- Chosen: count an older PR as a blocker only when `head.repo.full_name` (lowercased) equals `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` (lowercased). Pushing a branch to the base repository already requires write access, so a same-repository head is an authorized head.
- Alternatives considered: filtering on `author_association` (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR); using GitHub's `isCrossRepository` flag through a GraphQL listing.
- Why: `author_association` misses bot-authored same-repository PRs and needs extra rules. GraphQL would replace the REST listing the tests and the budget comment are built around. Comparing `full_name` uses data that is already fetched and is exactly what the finding recommends.

### D2 — Fail toward "not a blocker" when the head repo is unknown
- Chosen: an empty or null `head.repo` (deleted fork, malformed response) is never a blocker.
- Alternatives considered: treating an unknown head repo as a blocker (fail closed).
- Why: the train's documented contract is that it only ever delays review and may under-block but never over-block (script header, "Fail-open contract"). Treating unknowns as blockers would bring the DoS back through deleted forks.

### D3 — Skip foreign heads before the examination cap
- Chosen: put the foreign-head `continue` before the `examined` counter.
- Alternatives considered: putting it after the cap check, next to the file fetch.
- Why: otherwise 20 fork PRs could use up `MERGE_TRAIN_MAX_OLDER_PRS` and hide real same-repository blockers. They would also cost 20 wasted `pulls/N/files` calls (§14).

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: PR metadata from forks is attacker-controlled (head ref name, file list). After this change, only the base repository's own branches can affect queueing.
- Authorization: the gate and release surfaces are unchanged. Fork PRs still never reach `_mt_gate`, because review skips forks and the gate step requires `CAN_PUSH=true`.
- External-input validation: `head_repo` is only compared, never put into a command, path, or log line.
- Abuse cases covered:
  - A fork named `ai/issue-1` touching a hot file: no longer blocks anything.
  - A flood of forks to use up the cap: skipped before the cap, so this no longer works.
  - A case-varied fork name such as `Acme/Consumer`: a different owner is still a different repository, and lowercasing only normalizes case.
- Residual risk: a collaborator with write access can still hold the queue by opening a same-repository `ai/issue-*` PR. That is by design (lowest number first) and is outside the threat model.
- No secrets or money surfaces are involved.

## Risks and edge cases
- Existing tests build `_pr` without `head.repo`. Without the helper default, every older PR would become foreign and many queue tests would fail. The `_pr` default must be updated in the same change.
- A transferred or renamed base repository: `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` and `head.repo.full_name` both reflect the current name, so same-repository PRs still match.
- The fake `gh` in the tests applies the `--jq` filter with `jq -r`. The `//` operator and `tojson` both work there.
- No conflicts found between the issue and the codebase: line 223 is inside `_mt_blockers_for_into`, as the finding cites.

## Testing considerations
- Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m pytest tests/test_review_merge_train.py tests/test_review_dispatch_default_branch.py -q`.
- Run `bash -n scripts/review_merge_train.sh` and `shellcheck scripts/review_merge_train.sh`.
- Add the new tests (a)-(e) listed above, and make sure every existing test passes unchanged under the new `_pr` default.
